name: regex_anchored_line_start
description: The sprint-counting regex uses `^` anchor with the multiline flag (`m`) so that only headings starting at column 1 are matched, not inline prose references to sprints.

name: inline_sprint_references_not_counted
description: A spec containing '## Sprint 1' and '## Sprint 2' as line-start headings plus prose like 'builds on Sprint 3 features' or blockquoted '> ## Sprint 4' yields a total sprint count of 2.

name: standard_multiline_spec_counted_correctly
description: A spec with four '## Sprint N' headings each at column 1 on their own line yields a total sprint count of 4.

name: log_filename_timestamp_format
description: All conversation log filenames are prefixed with a timestamp matching the pattern YYYY.MM.DD-HH.MM.SS- (e.g., '2026.04.12-14.30.00-sprint-2-attempt-0-generator.md').

name: resume_does_not_overwrite_logs
description: When the harness resumes and re-runs the same sprint/attempt, a new log file is created with a different timestamp prefix; the original log file from the prior run remains on disk and is not overwritten or deleted.

name: contract_negotiation_logs_timestamped
description: Contract negotiation conversation logs follow the timestamped naming pattern (e.g., 'YYYY.MM.DD-HH.MM.SS-sprint-3-contract-negotiation.md').

name: all_agent_log_types_timestamped
description: Generator, Evaluator, Planner, and Documenter conversation logs all use the timestamp prefix format — no log file in .adhd/logs/ is written without a timestamp prefix.

name: timestamp_uses_configured_timezone
description: The timestamp in log filenames reflects the configured timezone (not UTC by default unless configured as UTC), consistent with the HH:MM:SS timestamps used in terminal output.

name: langfuse_span_names_aligned
description: Langfuse trace span names for agent conversations include the same timestamped identifier used in the log filename, enabling cross-referencing between log files and trace spans.

name: regex_fix_has_test_coverage
description: There is at least one test file covering the sprint-counting regex that tests: (1) standard headings are counted, (2) inline prose references are not counted, and (3) blockquoted or indented heading-like lines are not counted.

name: existing_contract_reused_on_resume
description: When the harness runs with --resume and `.adhd/contracts/sprint-N.json` already exists on disk, it loads and uses that contract without invoking contract negotiation agents (no Planner/Evaluator calls for that sprint's contract).

name: missing_contract_triggers_negotiation
description: When the harness runs with --resume and `.adhd/contracts/sprint-N.json` does NOT exist on disk, contract negotiation proceeds normally as if it were a fresh run.

name: loaded_contract_logged
description: When an existing contract is loaded from disk during resume, a log message is emitted that includes both the fact it was loaded from disk and the number of criteria in the contract (e.g., 'Loaded contract from disk for sprint 2 with 8 criteria').

name: contract_file_validation
description: When loading a contract from disk, the code validates that the file contains well-formed JSON matching the expected contract structure before using it. Malformed or empty contract files trigger negotiation rather than crashing.

name: parse_failure_writes_diagnostic_file
description: When parseContract fails to extract valid JSON from the evaluator's contract review response, a file `.adhd/logs/sprint-N-contract-parse-error.txt` is created containing the full raw unparseable text.

name: parse_failure_logs_truncated_preview
description: When parseContract falls back to the default contract due to a parse failure, a warning is logged to the console containing a truncated preview of the raw text (not the full 2000+ character blob).

name: successful_parse_no_diagnostic_file
description: When parseContract successfully extracts valid contract JSON, no `.adhd/logs/sprint-N-contract-parse-error.txt` file is created.

name: diagnostic_directory_created_on_demand
description: If `.adhd/logs/` does not exist when a parse error diagnostic needs to be written, the directory is created automatically (no crash on missing directory).

name: truncation_length_reasonable
description: The truncated preview logged to console on parse failure is capped at a reasonable length (200-500 characters) with an ellipsis or indicator showing it was truncated, so console output stays readable.

name: adhd_artifacts_committed_before_generator
description: Before each Generator agent invocation, all pending .adhd/ files (contracts, progress, feedback) are staged and committed with a commit message prefixed by '[adhd]'. The Generator starts with no uncommitted .adhd/ files in the working tree.

name: adhd_commit_message_format
description: The commit created for .adhd/ artifacts uses a message starting with '[adhd]' and includes the sprint number (e.g., '[adhd] Sprint 2: artifacts').

name: clean_working_tree_for_generator
description: After .adhd/ artifacts are committed and before the Generator session begins, running 'git status --porcelain' on .adhd/ paths returns no output, confirming a clean working tree.

name: revert_uses_git_reset_hard
description: The revertToCheckpoint function uses 'git reset --hard <sha>' instead of 'git revert --no-commit'. No calls to 'git revert' remain in the revert/rollback code path.

name: adhd_files_survive_revert
description: When revertToCheckpoint resets to a checkpoint SHA, .adhd/ files (progress.json, contracts/, feedback/) that were written after the checkpoint are preserved by stashing before reset and unstashing after. The files exist on disk with their pre-revert contents after the operation completes.

name: stash_unstash_error_handling
description: If git stash or unstash fails during revertToCheckpoint, the error is logged with a meaningful message and does not cause an unhandled exception. The revert still completes (reset --hard succeeds) even if stash restoration fails.

name: documenting_status_type
description: The HarnessProgress type's status union includes 'documenting' as a valid value alongside existing values like 'running', 'complete', etc. TypeScript compilation succeeds with this addition.

name: documenting_status_set_before_documenter
description: Before the Documenter agent is invoked, progress.json is written with status set to 'documenting'. This occurs after all sprints pass and before the Documenter starts its work.

name: complete_status_after_documenter
description: After the Documenter agent finishes (or is skipped), progress.json is updated to status 'complete'. The 'documenting' status is a transient state visible only while documentation is in progress.

name: no_regression_on_existing_revert_callers
description: All existing call sites that invoke revertToCheckpoint continue to work correctly with the new reset-based implementation. Resume flows that trigger checkpoint revert do not fail or leave the repo in a broken state.

name: commit_is_noop_when_no_changes
description: If there are no pending .adhd/ changes when the pre-Generator commit step runs (e.g., files were already committed), no empty commit is created. The harness handles the nothing-to-commit case gracefully.

name: terminal_bell_at_hitl_gates
description: All HITL gates (spec approval, contract approval, and any interactive prompts) write the terminal bell character (\x07) to stdout immediately before or alongside the prompt text

name: terminal_bell_on_fatal_error
description: When the harness encounters a fatal error that halts execution, a terminal bell character (\x07) is emitted alongside the error output

name: notify_flag_parsed
description: The CLI accepts a --notify flag. When provided, the resolved config includes a notify: true property. When omitted, it defaults to false

name: desktop_notification_with_notify_flag
description: When --notify is enabled and a HITL gate or fatal error occurs, the harness invokes the platform-appropriate desktop notification command (notify-send on Linux, osascript on macOS) with a descriptive message

name: no_desktop_notification_without_flag
description: When --notify is not provided, no desktop notification subprocess is spawned at HITL gates or errors — only the terminal bell is emitted

name: commit_adhd_flag_parsed
description: The CLI accepts --commit-adhd and --commit-adhd-logs flags. They are correctly parsed into the resolved config object with appropriate boolean properties

name: commit_adhd_creates_metadata_commit
description: When --commit-adhd is enabled and a sprint passes evaluation, a git commit is created containing .adhd/contracts/, .adhd/feedback/, .adhd/progress.json, and .adhd/spec.md with the message format '[adhd] Sprint N: contract + metadata'

name: commit_adhd_logs_includes_logs
description: When --commit-adhd-logs is enabled, the metadata commit additionally includes files from .adhd/logs/

name: commit_adhd_logs_implies_commit_adhd
description: When --commit-adhd-logs is provided without --commit-adhd, the resolved config sets commitAdhd to true (implication logic)

name: default_no_adhd_commits
description: When neither --commit-adhd nor --commit-adhd-logs is provided, no [adhd] metadata commits are created after sprints complete

name: app_starts_and_parses_new_flags
description: The harness entry point starts cleanly with the new flags (--notify, --commit-adhd, --commit-adhd-logs) without runtime errors, and --help output documents the new options

name: e2e_phantom_sprint_prevention
description: Running the harness against a spec with inline sprint references in prose, blockquotes, and acceptance criteria produces exactly the correct number of sprints matching only line-start headings — no phantom sprints are executed

name: e2e_resume_full_cycle
description: A full resume cycle works end-to-end: interrupting after sprint 2, resuming with --resume reuses existing contracts from disk, skips completed sprints, creates new timestamped log files without overwriting originals, and the checkpoint revert uses git reset --hard with .adhd/ stash/unstash

name: e2e_commit_adhd_flags
description: Running with --commit-adhd produces [adhd] commits containing contracts/feedback/progress/spec after each sprint, and --commit-adhd-logs additionally includes .adhd/logs/. Running without either flag produces no [adhd] metadata commits

name: e2e_notifications
description: All HITL gates (spec approval, contract review, evaluation review) emit terminal bell character. With --notify, desktop notifications are dispatched. Without --notify, no desktop notification commands are executed

name: progress_status_lifecycle
description: The progress.json status field transitions correctly through the full lifecycle: planning → generating → evaluating → (loop on failure) → documenting → complete, with 'documenting' appearing only when the Documenter agent is active

name: contract_parse_error_diagnostics
description: When contract parsing fails, a diagnostic file is written to .adhd/logs/sprint-N-contract-parse-error.txt with full raw text, a truncated preview is logged to console, and successful parses produce no diagnostic file

name: timestamp_log_consistency
description: All conversation log files (generator, evaluator, contract negotiation, documenter) use YYYY.MM.DD-HH.MM.SS prefix format. Multiple runs for the same sprint produce distinct timestamped files, and chronological ls ordering matches execution order

name: clean_working_tree_before_generator
description: Immediately before every Generator invocation, git status --porcelain shows no uncommitted .adhd/ files — they have been committed with an [adhd] prefix message

name: readme_cli_flags_documented
description: README or equivalent documentation describes --resume, --notify, --commit-adhd, and --commit-adhd-logs flags with usage examples and explains their interaction (e.g., --commit-adhd-logs implies --commit-adhd)

name: stage_usage_model_field_stored_exactly
description: When `recordStage` is called with a model string (e.g. `"claude-sonnet-4-20250514"`), the resulting `StageUsage` entry in tracker state has `model` equal to that exact string — no truncation, no transformation.

name: record_stage_model_parameter_required
description: `bun run typecheck` exits zero only when every `recordStage` call site passes a `model` argument. Removing the argument from any call site must produce a TypeScript type error. The parameter must not be optional or defaulted in the abstract interface signature.

name: shared_has_zero_llm_sdk_imports
description: A grep of all files under `shared/` for LLM-SDK import strings (e.g. `@anthropic-ai/`, `@ai-sdk/`, `openai`) returns zero matches after this sprint's changes are applied.

name: call_site_model_routing_correct
description: In a run with `--model-planner=A --model-generator=B --model-evaluator=C --model-documenter=D`, the persisted `.adhd/usage.json` shows: planner and planner-revision stages have `model: "A"`, generator stage has `model: "B"`, evaluator stage has `model: "C"`, documenter stage has `model: "D"`, contract-proposal stage has `model: "B"`, contract-review stage has `model: "C"`.

name: per_stage_summary_includes_model_column
description: The per-stage formatting pure helper, when invoked with a sample `StageUsage[]` containing at least two distinct models, returns strings where each row contains the stage's `model` value as a left-aligned text column immediately after the stage name and before the numeric columns. Asserted directly on returned `string[]` without log capture.

name: per_model_rollup_aggregation_correct
description: The pure rollup aggregator, when given `StageUsage[]` where model `"X"` appears in three stages with (inputTokens: 100, outputTokens: 50, costUsd: 0.01), (200, 80, 0.02), (300, 120, 0.03), returns a `ModelRollupRow` for `"X"` with inputTokens=600, outputTokens=250, costUsd=0.06. Asserted directly on the returned struct.

name: per_model_rollup_sorted_by_usd_descending
description: When the rollup aggregator is given stages across three models with total USD of 0.05, 0.20, and 0.10, the returned `ModelRollupRow[]` is ordered: 0.20, 0.10, 0.05. The terminal summary renders them in this order.

name: rollup_always_printed_even_single_model
description: When a run uses only one model (no per-agent overrides), the terminal summary still prints the per-model rollup section with exactly one row containing that model's aggregated totals. The section header is always present.

name: legacy_usage_json_loads_without_throw
description: Given a `.adhd/usage.json` whose stage entries omit the `model` field entirely, loading it via the tracker does not throw. Every loaded `StageUsage` has `model === "unknown"`. A subsequent `save()` rewrites the file with `model: "unknown"` on all legacy entries and the new model string on any newly-recorded entries.

name: save_load_round_trip_preserves_model
description: A tracker that records stages with models `"alpha"`, `"beta"`, and `"gamma"`, calls `save()`, then is replaced by a fresh tracker instance that loads the same file: every stage's `model` in the loaded state equals the originally-recorded string. No model value is lost, coerced, or defaulted to `"unknown"`.

name: usage_json_key_order_consistent
description: Each stage object in a freshly-written `.adhd/usage.json` has keys in the order: `stage`, `model`, `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `costUsd`, `durationMs`. Verified by reading the raw JSON string and checking key insertion order on at least one stage entry.

name: typecheck_and_lint_pass_clean
description: `bun run typecheck` and `bun run lint` (Biome) both exit with code 0 after all sprint changes. Zero new `any` casts are introduced in `shared/` or `harness-claude/` files touched by this sprint.

name: documentation_files_updated_correctly
description: README.md contains updated Cost tracking paragraph and Observability bullet mentioning per-model attribution. docs/INTERNALS.md Cost Tracking section describes both summary views and the persisted `model` field. docs/ROADMAP.md Part 1 §1.11 bullet 3 is extended; Parts 2 and 3 contain no new per-model tracking entry. CHANGELOG.md contains a new `## Phase 1.6: Observability Sharpening` section with `### Sprint 1 -- Per-Model Usage Tracking` immediately after the Phase 1.5 block, using identical heading levels and Features→bullets→Verified line ordering.

name: surfaces_round_trip
description: Writing a negotiated contract with surfaces to .adhd/contracts/sprint-N.json and re-reading it yields the identical surfaces array (same values, same membership, same order), with stable key ordering in the persisted JSON matching existing conventions.

name: legacy_contract_loads
description: Parsing a legacy contract JSON that has no surfaces field succeeds without throwing; the absent field is treated as unspecified (empty or undefined surface list), never crashing the run, and re-persisting it does not inject spurious values.

name: proposer_emits_surfaces
description: After contract negotiation runs, the resulting contract contains a non-empty surfaces array drawn only from the allowed vocabulary, reflecting the sprint's footprint. The proposer prompt explicitly instructs use of only the allowed vocabulary.

name: reviewer_validates_surfaces
description: Given a candidate contract whose surfaces is missing, empty, or contains an unknown token, the reviewer step produces an approved contract whose surfaces is present, non-empty, and contains only allowed vocabulary values: unknown tokens are dropped, and a contract that would end up with an empty surfaces list is rejected rather than approved.

name: app_starts_and_tests_pass
description: bun run typecheck, bun run lint, and bun test all pass cleanly. The harness still starts and negotiates a contract end-to-end without regressions to existing contract persistence.

name: graceful_degradation_no_crash
description: Model/tier resolution never throws and never crashes a run on odd input (missing env vars, empty/whitespace-only strings, unknown model overrides, mixed-case env values); it always produces concrete non-empty resolved model strings, consistent with the project's graceful-degradation convention. An unknown explicit override is passed through (or mapped) rather than causing an exception.

name: classifier_lives_in_surfaces_module
description: The new classification function is added to and exported from the existing shared/surfaces.ts module (no new parallel surface module is created), and it reuses the already-defined SURFACE_VOCABULARY, Surface type, and isSurface rather than redefining them.

name: returns_deduplicated_surface_set
description: Given a list of file path strings, the function returns the deduplicated set of Surface values touched. Backend source paths plus a test path classify to exactly {backend, tests}; frontend UI files plus a markdown file classify to exactly {frontend, docs}; duplicate paths or multiple paths of the same surface yield a single entry.

name: covers_all_six_surfaces
description: Default patterns correctly classify representative paths for every vocabulary token: db (migrations/schema/seed files), config (package manifests, lockfiles, dotfiles, CI config), tests (test directories or test-named files), frontend (.tsx/.jsx/.vue/.css and client UI dirs), backend (server-side source not frontend/tests), and docs (markdown/documentation). Covers both TS/Node and Python/Go style paths.

name: documented_single_surface_precedence
description: Each path maps to at most one surface via an explicit, documented evaluation order. A test file with a frontend extension (e.g. a .test.tsx file) resolves to tests only, not frontend, and this precedence is verified by a test.

name: deterministic_order_independent
description: Classifying the same path list in different orders yields an identical resulting set; results are deterministic across repeated calls with no dependence on input ordering.

name: never_throws_on_odd_input
description: The function never throws on degenerate input — empty path list returns an empty set; empty strings, whitespace, paths with no extension, and unrecognized paths are silently omitted from the result rather than causing an error (mirroring normalizeSurfaces' best-effort contract).

name: purity_no_io_or_sdk
description: The function performs no git, filesystem, or network calls and has no side effects — it operates solely on the provided path strings. shared/surfaces.ts contains zero Claude SDK imports, preserving the shared/ boundary.

name: full_unit_test_coverage
description: tests/ contains unit tests for the classifier covering every acceptance scenario: multi-surface lists, each of the six surfaces, the .test.tsx precedence case, empty input, order-independence, and odd/unclassifiable input. All tests pass under `bun test`.

name: clean_typecheck_lint_build
description: `bun run typecheck` reports no errors, `bun run lint` passes with no new violations, and the full `bun test` suite (including pre-existing Sprint 1 tests) passes — the module integrates cleanly with the existing codebase end-to-end.

name: changed_files_helper_returns_paths
description: A new name-only changed-files helper in shared/diff.ts returns the list of changed path strings for an attempt (via `git diff --name-only beforeSha..HEAD`), sitting alongside computeDiffSection and reusing the same workDir/beforeSha/attempt inputs.

name: changed_files_helper_graceful_degradation
description: The changed-files helper returns undefined (or empty) on attempt 0, empty beforeSha, or any git failure, and never throws — matching computeDiffSection's degradation contract.

name: adhd_metadata_excluded
description: Paths under `.adhd/` are filtered out of the changed-file list before classification, so the committed metadata commit between beforeSha and HEAD never influences the coverage decision (verified even with a path that would otherwise classify to a surface).

name: coverage_gate_fails_on_uncovered_surface
description: When the contract declares surfaces (e.g. backend + frontend) but the classified changed files cover only a subset, the attempt fails before any Evaluator SDK call, and the overallSummary names exactly the declared surfaces that were not touched.

name: evaluator_skipped_no_cost_on_failure
description: On a coverage failure the Evaluator is never invoked (zero AI cost), and a normal-level log line states the check ran, that it failed, and that the Evaluator was skipped to save cost.

name: coverage_pass_runs_evaluator
description: When the changed files cover all declared surfaces, the coverage check passes and the Evaluator runs normally, unchanged from prior behavior.

name: failure_eval_result_shape_matches_lint_gate
description: A coverage failure produces an EvalResult with the same shape the --lint-gate failure produces (passed:false, scores:{}, per-criterion feedback entries scored 0, an overallSummary), is persisted via writeFeedback, calls attemptSpan.end(...), and `continue`s the retry loop — identical control flow to the lint gate.

name: retry_feedback_propagates_missed_surface
description: After a coverage failure on a non-final attempt, the next Generator invocation receives the failure feedback identifying the missed surface(s), via the same retry-feedback path as a normal failed attempt.

name: skip_when_no_declared_surfaces_or_no_diff
description: The gate is skipped (Evaluator proceeds as before, no crash) when the contract declares no/empty surfaces, or when the changed-file list cannot be computed (missing beforeSha, git failure, empty list).

name: gate_ordering_documented
description: When --lint-gate is also active, the relative order of the two cheap gates is documented in code/comments, and whichever fails first short-circuits to a failed attempt without invoking the Evaluator.

name: clean_build_and_tests
description: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, and `bun test` all pass; new unit tests cover the changed-files helper (including degradation and .adhd/ exclusion) and the gate's pass/fail/skip branches.

name: default_limits_resolved
description: With no flags or env vars set, resolveConfig produces a ResolvedConfig where maxFeatures=3, maxCriteria=10, and maxSurfaces=2, sourced from DEFAULT_CONFIG.

name: cli_flags_override_defaults
description: Passing --max-features 2, --max-criteria 5, or --max-surfaces 1 results in the corresponding resolved field taking the flag value, parsed via parseInt as an integer (not a string), overriding the default.

name: env_var_resolution_and_precedence
description: When MAX_FEATURES/MAX_CRITERIA/MAX_SURFACES env vars are set without a corresponding CLI flag, the env value is used; when both a flag and env var are present for the same limit, the CLI flag wins. Precedence matches the existing maxSprints/maxRetries shape (flag > env > .adhd/.env > default).

name: validation_rejects_invalid_limits
description: validateConfig throws a clear, specific error for non-positive or non-integer limit values (e.g. --max-criteria 0, negative, or a non-numeric string), with a message consistent in style with the existing threshold/max-sprints/max-retries validation errors.

name: help_output_lists_new_flags
description: printHelp output (driven by CLI_FLAG_HELP) includes all three new flags (--max-features, --max-criteria, --max-surfaces) each with a human-readable description and stated default value.

name: type_definitions_consistent
description: The three limit fields exist on both HarnessConfig and ResolvedConfig in shared/types.ts with correct types, so validateConfig (typed against HarnessConfig) and downstream Sprint 5 consumers can reference them without type errors.

name: no_enforcement_this_sprint
description: The limits are only resolved, exposed, and validated; negotiation and contract parsing behavior is unchanged this sprint (no trimming or rejection of contracts based on these limits is introduced).

name: app_starts_and_typechecks_cleanly
description: bun run typecheck passes with no errors, the harness starts cleanly, and the existing test suite (bun test) continues to pass alongside the new config tests.

name: shared_has_no_sdk_imports
description: All new config logic stays in shared/config.ts and shared/types.ts with zero Claude SDK imports, respecting the shared/ SDK-independence boundary.

name: limits_threaded_into_negotiation
description: NegotiateContractOptions in shared/orchestration/types.ts gains maxFeatures, maxCriteria, maxSurfaces, and the agents.negotiateContract call site in runSprintLoop (shared/orchestration/harness.ts) passes config.maxFeatures/maxCriteria/maxSurfaces while keeping proposalModel/reviewModel/usage and the withTransientRetry wrapper intact.

name: reviewer_prompt_is_limit_aware_builder
description: The static CONTRACT_NEGOTIATION_EVALUATOR_PROMPT becomes a builder (e.g. buildContractReviewPrompt({maxFeatures,maxCriteria,maxSurfaces})) in shared/prompts.ts that injects the active limit numbers, instructs the reviewer to reject over-limit contracts and return a narrowed one keeping highest-priority items, while preserving the existing surface-vocabulary rules; the harness-claude/contract.ts call site builds it with the threaded limits.

name: pure_ceiling_check_and_trim
description: A pure, side-effect-free function in shared/ (new shared/contract-limits.ts or an extension of shared/surfaces.ts) takes a SprintContract plus the three limits, reports which limits are exceeded, and returns a trimmed contract keeping the first N features, first N criteria, and first N declared surfaces routed through normalizeSurfaces; it never throws on odd input and never performs git/filesystem/network I/O.

name: features_capped
description: Given default limits and a proposed contract with 5 features, the finalized contract has at most maxFeatures (3) features; likewise 12 criteria is reduced to at most maxCriteria (10) and 3 declared surfaces to at most maxSurfaces (2).

name: enforcement_on_final_parsed_contract
description: Enforcement in negotiateContract (harness-claude/contract.ts) runs after the reviewText.trim()==="APPROVED" ? proposalText : reviewText selection and parseContract, so an oversized proposal that the reviewer returned APPROVED on is still narrowed/trimmed to within all limits.

name: bounded_single_narrowing_round
description: If the parsed contract still exceeds any limit, exactly one additional reviewer narrowing round (using the limit-aware prompt) is triggered; if still over after that single round, the deterministic pure trim is applied so the loop never recurses indefinitely and the Generator never receives an over-budget contract.

name: custom_limits_respected
description: Given custom limits via --max-features/--max-criteria/--max-surfaces, the non-default values are the ones injected into the reviewer prompt and applied by the programmatic check; a contract already within all limits is left unchanged with no extra round run.

name: narrowing_observability
description: When a contract is narrowed or trimmed, a normal-level HARNESS log line reports before/after counts for features, criteria, and surfaces in the existing plain-English voice; deterministic trims additionally log a clear warning that trimming occurred.

name: operational_integrity
description: bun run typecheck, bun run lint, and bun test all pass; shared/ remains free of Claude SDK imports; the AgentRunners DI boundary is respected (pure ceiling logic lives in shared/, SDK/prompt-building enforcement lives in harness-claude/contract.ts); the harness still starts and negotiates a contract end-to-end.

name: ceiling_logic_unit_coverage
description: The pure ceiling check/trim has dedicated unit tests covering: under-limit (unchanged), over each individual limit, over all limits simultaneously, surface trimming with duplicate/unknown tokens dropped via normalizeSurfaces preserving declared order, and empty/odd input never throwing.

name: named_tier_constants_replace_stale_default
description: Model IDs are defined once as named tier constants (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a single place (shared/models.ts or a delineated block in shared/config.ts) using current generally-available model IDs. The literal string 'claude-opus-4-6' no longer appears as the uniform default anywhere in the codebase; all former CLAUDE_MODEL call sites (the resolveConfig fallback and the --model help text) reference the named constants instead.

name: per_agent_default_matrix
description: With no model flags or env vars set, resolveConfig yields resolvedModelPlanner = Opus tier, resolvedModelGenerator = Sonnet tier, resolvedModelEvaluator = Opus tier, and resolvedModelDocumenter = Haiku tier. Each resolved field is a concrete non-empty string.

name: resolution_precedence_per_agent
description: Precedence is enforced per agent: an explicit --model-<agent>/MODEL_<AGENT> override wins over an explicit uniform --model/CLAUDE_MODEL, which wins over the per-agent tier default. The matrix only applies when the user set neither a per-agent override nor a uniform model. An explicit uniform --model X resolves all four agents to X (matrix not applied), and an explicit --model-generator override wins over the Sonnet matrix default. Resolution distinguishes a user-supplied uniform model from a fallback to the default constant.

name: evaluator_ge_generator_invariant_warning
description: When the resolved configuration would place the Evaluator tier below the Generator tier, a clear HARNESS-tagged warning naming the invariant is emitted exactly once and the run is NOT hard-failed. Explicit per-agent overrides still take effect; the warning is advisory only. When Evaluator tier ≥ Generator tier, no such warning is emitted.

name: model_contract_knob
description: A new optional --model-contract CLI flag plus matching MODEL_CONTRACT env var is plumbed through NegotiateContractOptions. When set, all negotiation SDK calls — proposal, review, and the F5 bounded narrowing round — use the specified model. When unset, negotiation preserves the existing inherited split (proposal on the Generator model, review and narrowing on the Evaluator model). The addition is additive and does not disturb the F5 size-limit option fields.

name: honest_startup_model_log
description: On startup, runHarness prints the resolved model for all four agents including the Documenter (which was previously omitted), reflecting the actual per-agent matrix rather than a single Model: line, in the plain HARNESS voice with each line standing alone.

name: help_documents_matrix_and_flags
